Single-stage analysis of several trials

Source: R/single_stage.R
analyze_single_stage.Rd

Fits all trials (locations, environments) together in one mixed model and gives the genotype adjusted means across trials, to compare with (or use instead of) the two-stage analysis of analyze_two_stage(): $$y = \mu + \text{trial} + \text{genotype} + \text{rep(trial)} + \text{block(rep, trial)} + \text{genotype} \times \text{trial} + e,$$ with trials and genotypes fixed, and replicates, blocks and the genotype-by-trial interaction random (fitted with 'lme4'). Genotype means average the trial effects with equal weights. Without 'lme4' the model is fitted with all effects fixed and no genotype-by-trial term.

Usage

analyze_single_stage(
  data,
  response,
  genotype_col = "accession",
  location_col = "trial_name",
  replicate_col = NULL,
  block_col = NULL,
  genotype_by_location = c("random", "none"),
  spatial = FALSE,
  row_col = "row",
  col_col = "col",
  spatial_nseg = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per plot, e.g. from breedbase_phenotypes().

response

Name of the numeric response column.

genotype_col, location_col

Genotype and trial (location) columns.

replicate_col, block_col

Optional replicate and block columns; by default "rep"/"replicate" and "block" when the data have them.

genotype_by_location

"random" (default) or "none".

spatial

Logical. Fit the single-stage model with 'SpATS' (needs the field row and col of every plot).

row_col, col_col

Field row and column columns (for spatial = TRUE).

spatial_nseg

Optional number of P-spline segments, c(col, row).

Value

An object of class single_stage_analysis: adjusted_means (ranked, with standard errors and the number of trials), adjusted_means_vcov, variance_components, plot_results (fitted values and residuals), diagnostics and the fitted model.

Details

With spatial = TRUE the model is fitted with 'SpATS': genotypes and trials fixed, replicates within trials fixed, blocks and the genotype-by-trial interaction random, and a smooth P-spline surface over the field rows and columns. SpATS fits one surface per model, so the trials are placed side by side in one coordinate system, separated by empty columns: each trial keeps its own spatial trend and the trends do not run from one trial into another.

One error variance is shared by all trials here; when trials differ much in precision, the weighted two-stage analysis is the better choice (Möhring and Piepho, 2009).

References

Möhring, J. and Piepho, H.-P. (2009). Comparison of weighting in two-stage analysis of plant breeding trials. Crop Science 49, 1977-1988. doi:10.2135/cropsci2009.02.0083

Examples

sites <- c("North", "South")
met <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:2, function(i) {
  d <- augmented_row_column_design(paste0("G", 1:108), paste0("C", 1:4), 12, 12, 4, 4,
                                   n_candidates = 5, seed = i)$design
  d$location <- sites[i]
  d
}))
set.seed(1)
g <- stats::setNames(stats::rnorm(112, sd = 3), c(paste0("G", 1:108), paste0("C", 1:4)))
met$yield <- 50 + g[met$all_entries] + stats::rnorm(nrow(met))
one <- analyze_single_stage(met, "yield", genotype_col = "all_entries", location_col = "location")
#> boundary (singular) fit: see help('isSingular')
one
